newsitem.title: MEXICO: Tribasa, Burlington Northern preparing railway bid.
newsitem.headline: Tribasa, Burlington Northern preparing railway bid.

text.p: Builder Grupo Tribasa and U.S. railroad company Burlington Northern Sante Fe have agreed to join forces in a bid for the privatization of a Mexican railway, a Tribasa official said on Friday.
The bid for the Pacific-Norte line will be led by Tribasa, the official, who declined to be identified, told Reuters.
"The agreement (with Burlington) is to bid for the Pacifico-Norte line. Still to be defined is if they will participate as an equity partner or a commercial partner," the official said.
Tribasa and partners RailTex Inc and Impulsora Tlaxcalteca created a consortium to bid for the nation's shorter railway lines and the 6,000 km Pacifico-Norte route.
Before the inclusion of the new U.S. partner, Tribasa owned half the consortium's shares with its partners holding 25 percent each.
The Pacific-Norte line connects cargo centers such as Manzanillo, Guadalajara and Culiacan that connects with U.S. border states, where Burlington Northern and Union Pacific have lines.
The government has not yet published the guidelines for the bidding, but generally restricts foreign ownership of privatized assets to a minority stake.
